subject: Trade-in credit vs bundle: transition economics and escape hatch
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@orchidai.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on competitor trade-in credit + migration support

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re evaluating a change from our current vendor (NimbleDeep) and they’ve offered a fairly aggressive trade-in: $250k in credits applied over 12 months plus 3 weeks of dedicated migration engineering.

Before we escalate internally I wanted to check what flexibility Redwood would have on:
- a trade-in or transition credit (one-time vs amortized)
- guaranteed onboarding engineering hours / escalation SLA for the first 90 days
- whether credits can be used against committed Dedicated capacity or only hosted usage

We’re targeting a decision by mid-June. If there’s a short term bridge (60–90 day) credit or a blended package (credit + extended onboarding) that makes the business case cleaner for us.

Appreciate a quick read — happy to hop on a short call.

—Samir
Head of Platform — Orchid AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on competitor trade-in credit + migration support

Samir —

Thanks for sharing the NimbleDeep terms. Quick thoughts (high level):

1) Trade-in vs amortized credits: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit or amortize it across a 6–12 month committed term. For your scale, a staggered credit tied to deployment milestones usually lands better with finance.

2) Engineering hours: we can commit up to 4 dedicated sprints (~6 engineer-weeks) as part of a jumpstart package, with an SLA-backed escalation path for P1s during the first 90 days. We typically attach a small implementation SOW for deeper integrations.

3) Commitment applicability: credits are normally applied to hosted usage. For Dedicated (reserved) we can structure an offset to the first quarter invoice or a capacity credit if you want guaranteed throughput pricing.

I’m looping in Laura (commercial) and Priyom (technical GTM) to put numbers together and outline two options: (A) 90-day bridge credit + limited onboarding (B) full trade-in amortized over a 12-month commit + expanded engineering.

Can you confirm the target ARR and whether Orchid would consider a 6–12 month committed minimum for the better credit? That will change the math.

Best,
Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on competitor trade-in credit + migration support

Samir —

Attached is a short economics memo and two proposal structures (attached PDFs):

Option 1 — Short bridge
- 60-day usage credit equal to 40% of the first-month projected runrate (one-time).
- 3 weeks of dedicated onboarding engineering (remote) + 24/7 escalation on P1s for 30 days.
- No committed minimum required.

Option 2 — Committed offset (best value)
- $200k trade-in credit amortized as credits across 12 months tied to a 12-month Dedicated commitment at a guaranteed throughput tier.
- 6 engineer-weeks of onboarding (includes on-site if required) + P1 SLA coverage for 90 days.
- Early-exit escape hatch: 60% of unused credits refunded as pro-rated invoice credit if cancellation during months 3–6, 30% refund months 7–12.

Notes on implementation costs that impact the net value:
- Data egress and replay costs: can be capped in the SOW for the first 30 days to avoid surprise charges.
- Repo/infra compatibility: small adapter work (2–3 engineer-days) for their custom pre/post-processing (we included as part of onboarding for Option 2).

I also added a migration timeline spreadsheet with milestones and gating criteria (SOW-transition-timeline.xlsx).

If you prefer, we can present Option 2 with a more aggressive initial credit in exchange for a 24-month commit — we can run that sensitivity quickly.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orchard_Econ_Memo_v1.pdf (stub), Orchid_Migration_Credit_Proposal_v2.pdf (stub), SOW-transition-timeline.xlsx (stub)

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on competitor trade-in credit + migration support

Laura / Marcus —

Thanks — the memo is helpful. A few clarifying points from our procurement and engineering:
- Procurement prefers amortized credits that apply against committed spend (Option 2 style), but they would want a stronger escape hatch (we'd ask for a 75% pro-rate refund months 3–6).
- Engineering is focused on guaranteed onboarding bandwidth and an SLA for latency regressions for the first 90 days. On-site weeks would be nice but not required.
- They asked whether credits can be applied to both hosted usage and initial Dedicated payments (to cover capacity reservation).

Bottom line: we’re leaning towards Option 2 if you can: (a) move the amortized credit to $250k, (b) provide 6 engineer-weeks, (c) improve the escape hatch to the 75% refund window for months 3–6, and (d) allow credits to apply to the initial Dedicated invoice.

We can get legal and procurement to expedite if commercial agrees in principle.

—Samir
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchidai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on competitor trade-in credit + migration support

Samir —

Short answer: we can do a revised Option 2 to meet your asks with final approval from finance and legal. Here's the guardrails we propose: 

- Credit: $225k amortized across 12 months (higher than normal but within approval range).
- Onboarding: 6 engineer-weeks (remote) + a guaranteed 5 business-day P1 response SLA for the first 90 days.
- Escape hatch: 75% pro-rated refund months 3–6, 40% months 7–12.
- Credits: eligible to be applied to the first Dedicated invoice (limited to the first quarter) or hosted usage — not both. You pick which to apply against at kickoff.
- Data egress cap: we will cap replay/egress charges at an agreed dollar limit for the first 30 days in the SOW.

Laura will send the redlined commercial proposal and the SOW for legal review by EOD tomorrow. If that looks good, we can route an exec approval request for the $225k credit and aim to sign DocuSign by next week.

If you want the full $250k, we can consider it in exchange for a 24-month committed term — happy to model that for you.

Next steps: Laura to share final proposal, Marcus to request finance approval, Priyom to confirm onboarding resource availability.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
